narrative.title: Balancing Shelves Along One Reading Order
narrative.scenario: A library must distribute a fixed sequence of volumes onto m reading desks. The sequence cannot be reordered, every desk gets a non-empty consecutive block, and the fairest split minimizes the page count on the most-loaded desk. Compute that minimized maximum load, or report that there are more desks than volumes.
narrative.inputFormat: An integer N, an array A of N positive page counts (in fixed order), and an integer M, the number of students.
narrative.outputFormat: The minimum possible value of the maximum pages assigned to any student, or -1 when M > N.
constraints: Blocks must be contiguous and every student gets at least one book

complexity.optimalTime: O(N log S), where S is the total page count

testCases.explanation: Splitting after the third volume balances 113 against 90, and every other split leaves a heavier desk.
Blocks 25+46, 28, 49 and 24 cap the load at 71, the best the order allows.

hintLevels: Level 1: A load cap either permits a valid split or does not, and raising the cap never breaks a valid split - monotonic again.
Level 2: For a candidate cap, walk the fixed order filling one desk at a time and open a new desk whenever the next volume would overflow it.
Level 3: The search range runs from the largest single volume to the sum of all pages, the desk count must not exceed M, and more desks than volumes is the explicit -1 case.
